To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a condensate of helium nuclei in an electron gas in the core of a white dwarf is a strongly coupled system, (2) the effective potential is strongly suppressed due to quantum screening and (3) this screening is due to the subtraction of a phonon.

(1) the effective Lagrangian method is an efficient way to study the charged condensate, and (2) the strong screening is due to a cancellation due to the phonon subtraction, and (3) the one-loop quantum correction is also suppressed by this cancellation.

(i) the effective Lagrangian of charged condensate in a fermionic background is a sum of a free Lagrangian for the phonons plus a free Lagrangians for the charged scalar field, and (ii) the screened potential of a charged impurity has a quantum correction that is smaller by a factor of the phonon mass, and therefore is negligible.
